name: 80K Hours Upskilling Resources
current_details: A curated list of 67 resources for upskilling in technical AI safety research, compiled by 80,000 Hours in consultation with their advisors. Covers field overviews (AISafety.com, Anthropic's recommended research agendas, Redwood's control work), technical courses (ARENA, BlueDot Impact, Karpathy's Zero to Hero, Jacob Hilton's Deep Learning Curriculum), project ideas and open problems in evals and mech interp, advice from researchers like Neel Nanda, Ethan Perez and Richard Ngo, fellowships (Anthropic AI Safety Fellowship, MATS, Constellation Astra, LASR Labs, SPAR, Pivotal, ARENA Cambridge, ERA, CHAI, Global AI Safety Fellowship), and profiles of key technical AI safety organisations (Apollo, CHAI, FAR AI, METR, Palisade, Redwood, ARC, AE Studio, Conjecture). Written by Matt Beard, first published June 4th, 2025 and last updated September 15th, 2025.

name: 80K Hours AI Safety Career Review
current_details: A comprehensive 80,000 Hours career review (by Benjamin Hilton, last updated August 2024, first published June 2023) on AI safety technical research, covering two main paths: empirical AI safety — open to strong software engineers who can apply for research contributor roles immediately, even without an ML background — and theoretical AI safety, suited to those with very strong maths/theoretical CS backgrounds or the ability to get into a top 10 ML PhD program. It covers why the work is high impact, downsides and risk of harm, earnings, predicting personal fit, learning resources, whether to do a PhD, job application strategies, and key organisations. This is a permanent resource page with no application deadline, linked to 80,000 Hours' job board, free AI career advisor chatbot, and free 1-on-1 advising.

name: AISafety.com Events & Training
current_deadline: Updated continuously — next listed deadline 28 Sep 2026
current_details: AISafety.com maintains a continuously updated directory of 101 AI safety training programs — fellowships, bootcamps, and courses, online and in person — alongside 32 events, plus job (541), funding (56), and community (251) listings. It currently lists 47 upcoming training programs, filterable by type, focus (technical/governance/general), entry bar, stipend, length, and location, with durations from 4 days to 1 year. Open applications include Lens Academy's Alignment Theory of Deep Learning, the LAISH Foundations of AI Safety Fellowship, Leaf's Dilemmas and Dangers in AI, AI Security Bootcamp London (Dec 2026), LawAI's EU Law and Summer 2027 fellowships, the December 2026 Iliad Fellowship, the Foresight Fellowship 2028, and the Anthropic AI Safety Fellows Program (Jan 2027).

structured.stipend: Varies — many listings include stipends or covered expenses
structured.location: Online and in person (US, UK, EU, Asia)

name: AISafety.com Self-Study
current_details: A curated directory of 28 self-study curricula and reading lists for learning AI safety independently, spanning general introductions (BlueDot's Future of AI and Intro to Transformative AI, AI Risk Fundamentals, DeepMind's 75-minute AGI Safety Short Course, AI Safety Atlas, AISES, ERIC, Intro to Cooperative AI), technical alignment training (ARENA, Introduction to ML Safety, Agent Foundations, Iliad Intensive, Harvard CS 2881, Stanford's Introduction to AI Safety, UChicago XLab AI Security Guide, Meridian's 16-lecture Language Models and Intelligent Agentic Systems) and governance/strategy material (ENAIS Deep Dive, AGI Strategy, MATS strategy curriculum, Economics of Transformative AI, Redwood's AI Futurism Reading List). Each entry is tagged by focus and format (curriculum vs. reading list), with no application process or deadline. It is a permanently maintained reference hub run by AISafety.com, alongside their directories of jobs, funding, events and communities.

name: Apart Research Hackathons
current_details: Apart Research runs monthly online research sprints (hackathons) open to anyone worldwide, plus two fellowship tracks: the Apart Fellowship, which turns hackathon ideas into published research, and Partnered Fellowships, where participants apply to existing project proposals with mentorship from leading researchers. Its research focuses on manipulation and dark patterns in frontier AI systems, in collaboration with the EU AI Office and AI providers. Programs have engaged 8,000+ participants from 26 nationalities across 50+ sprints, with the top 2% joining fellowships that have published at NeurIPS, ICLR, ACL, and EMNLP.

structured.location: Remote (org based in Denver, CO, USA)

name: BlueDot Impact
current_details: BlueDot Impact is a non-profit AI safety talent accelerator with staff in San Francisco, London, and remote, running free online courses, funding via grants, and intensive in-person programs. Since 2022 they've trained 10,000+ professionals, and 25% of graduates land impactful roles within six months at places like Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and the UK AI Security Institute. The entry point is the free, self-paced 2-hour "The Future of AI" course with no application required, followed by longer courses, grants, in-person programs, and weekly global events.

name: Google DeepMind: AGI Safety Short Course
current_details: A free, self-paced introductory course on AGI safety from Google DeepMind's safety research team, consisting of ~75 minutes of short recorded talks and exercises plus an accompanying slide deck and exercise workbook. It covers the path to superhuman capabilities, risks from deliberate planning and instrumental subgoals, how misaligned goals arise (specification gaming vs. goal misgeneralization), DeepMind's technical alignment approach (amplified oversight, robust training & monitoring, security & control, interpretability, safer design patterns, alignment stress tests), and its governance approach including frontier safety practices and dangerous capability evaluations. Aimed at students, researchers and professionals who want an accessible one-hour introduction to AI alignment.

name: MATS Slack #opportunities
current_details: Contract work, facilitation gigs, paper reviews, and collaboration opportunities from the MATS community.

name: Outsider's Roadmap to AI Safety (LessWrong)
current_details: A comprehensive guide published in July 2025 for professionals transitioning into AI safety research from technical backgrounds such as software engineering, physics, or data science. Covers three critical domains: interpretability research (reverse-engineering AI systems to understand their inner workings), alignment research (ensuring AI systems remain beneficial and share human values), and AI control & governance (technical policy for advanced systems). Written by someone actively making the transition, synthesizing insights from Neel Nanda's mechanistic interpretability resources, 80,000 Hours career research, and the broader alignment community, with practical advice on evolving roles (the shift from separate research engineers/scientists toward 'full-stack researchers'), required skills, and pathways for newcomers to contribute meaningfully to the field.

name: Anthropic Fellows Program
current_details: The Anthropic Fellows Program funds and mentors engineers and researchers to tackle Anthropic's highest-priority AI safety questions — scalable oversight, adversarial robustness, AI control, model organisms, mechanistic interpretability, AI security, and model welfare. Fellows spend 4 months on empirical research with an Anthropic mentor, receiving a weekly stipend of $3,850 USD (£2,310 GBP / $4,300 CAD) plus ~$15K/month in compute funding. No PhD, prior ML experience, or published papers required; over 80% of first-cohort fellows produced papers and over 40% joined Anthropic full-time.

name: CAIS AI & Society Fellowship
current_details: A fully-funded, three-month in-person fellowship at CAIS in San Francisco for scholars in economics, law, international relations, and adjacent disciplines to pursue self-directed research on AI's societal impacts. Fellows receive a $25,000 stipend plus covered travel and daily lunch and dinner, and take part in guest speaker events, workshops, and a closing research presentation where they share interim outputs. Open to professors, PhD/JD holders or students, and researchers with equivalent experience; no prior AI research required.

name: CBAI Summer Research Fellowship
current_deadline: Rolling — Expression of Interest open for Spring 2026
current_details: CBAI's Research Fellowship is an intensive, fully-funded ten-week program in Cambridge, Massachusetts for researchers advancing careers in technical AI safety, AI governance, or technical governance. Fellows receive an $8,000 stipend, housing for non-local participants, weekday meals, 24/7 Harvard Square workspace, up to $10,000 in compute credits, and weekly 1–2 hours of mentorship from researchers at Harvard, MIT, Google DeepMind, UK AI Security Institute, CNAS, RAND and others. Open to undergraduates, master's and PhD students, postdocs, and early-career professionals (18+; OPT/CPT accepted but no visa sponsorship), with an extension program of up to 4 months available.

name: ERA Fellowship (Cambridge)
current_deadline: Closed — Winter 2027 cycle runs Jan 18 – Mar 26, 2027
current_details: The ERA:AI Fellowship is a 10-week intensive research programme in Cambridge, UK for people working on technical AI safety, AI governance, and technical AI governance. Fellows receive a competitive stipend, meals during working hours, covered transport and visas, dedicated research management, and a generous compute budget, plus mentorship from experts across government, academia and industry. The cohort experience includes 30+ events and a community of 200+ alumni now at organisations like the UK AI Security Institute, GovAI, RAND, DeepMind and Anthropic.

name: Global AI Safety Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed — final deadline was 31 December 2024; expressions of interest accepted for the second iteration
current_details: Impact Academy's Global AI Safety Fellowship is a fully funded research program placing exceptional STEM talent with leading AI safety organisations including CHAI (UC Berkeley), Conjecture, FAR.AI, and the UK AI Safety Institute. Fellows work full-time for up to 6 months (or longer) and receive up to $30,000, plus an optional fully-funded AI safety bootcamp, mentorship, 1:1 coaching, and visa/logistics support. A cohort of 10–20 fellows is selected worldwide via a two-phase, 4–6 week process requiring demonstrated ML/deep learning knowledge, programming experience, and scholastic excellence.

structured.location: In-person preferred (US or UK partner orgs); hybrid/remote possible
structured.program_dates: Flexible start; offers expected from March 2025 onwards

name: Iliad Intensive / Fellowship
current_details: Iliad matures AI safety as a theoretical and experimental science through research incubation (AIXI Labs, Principia, Stormglass, XOR Labs), training, and fieldbuilding. The Iliad Intensive is a 4-week taught program in foundational AI alignment for researchers and technical practitioners with strong mathematical backgrounds, run monthly at venues including Lighthaven, LISA, and Mox; the Iliad Fellowship is a 3-month mentored research program for researchers pursuing mathematical and theoretical AI safety work. Applications are currently open for the Nov 2026 Intensive at LISA (Nov 2–27, 2026), while the Aug/Sep/Oct 2026 Intensives and Fall 2026 Fellowship are closed.

structured.program_dates: Nov 2–27, 2026 (Nov Intensive, LISA); Sep 7–Dec 4, 2026 (Fall Fellowship, LISA)

name: MATS (ML Alignment Theory Scholars)
current_deadline: Winter 2027 scholar applications are closed; mentor applications open for Winter & Summer 2027
current_details: MATS is an independent research fellowship that connects talented researchers with top mentors in AI alignment, transparency, and security. Fellows conduct research for 12 weeks at offices in Berkeley, CA and London, UK, with the opportunity to apply for an additional 6–12 month funded extension. MATS also runs a Residency for long-horizon AI safety research, and mentor applications are currently open for the Winter and Summer 2027 cohorts.

name: AE Studio — AI Alignment Research Grants
current_details: The AI Alignment Foundation (formerly AE Studio) provides research funding plus dedicated engineering teams to accelerate high-risk, high-reward alignment research beyond mechanistic interpretability, evals, and control. It targets alignment researchers with ideas their current institutional funding won't cover, as well as technical experts from other fields (cognitive neuroscience, mathematics, physics) whose perspectives could open new directions. Engineering teams can execute proposals with as little as one hour per week of the researcher's time, and applicants describe a first experiment a good engineering team could run in 1–2 weeks.

structured.location: Marina Del Rey, CA (remote applications welcome)

name: Pivotal Research Fellowship
current_details: A 15-week full-time, in-person AI safety research fellowship in London (18 January – 30 April 2027) hosted at the London Initiative for Safe AI (LISA), featuring weekly 1-on-1 mentorship from established researchers, dedicated research managers, workshops, and speaker sessions. Fellows receive a £6,000–£8,000 stipend (Senior Fellows with a PhD or strong track record get £8,000) plus travel, £2,400 housing support for non-London fellows, weekday meals, and compute. Open to anyone 18 or older committed to making AI go well regardless of academic background; the process involves a written application, video interview, mentor work task, and final interview.

name: Second Look Research (UChicago XLab)
current_details: Second Look Research is a project of the Existential Risk Lab (XLab) at the University of Chicago that produces open-source replications of load-bearing empirical results in AI safety. The site hosts a Replications Fellowship for researchers who want to independently verify influential findings, alongside published replication work and a form for community members to request specific replications. No application dates or stipend details are listed on the landing page.

name: SPAR
current_deadline: Fall 2026 closed — Spring 2027 applications open around December 2026
current_details: SPAR (run by Kairos) is a 3-month, part-time, remote research fellowship pairing aspiring AI safety, security and policy researchers with 240+ experienced mentors. Mentees commit 5–40 hours/week, produce real research that has reached ICML, ICLR, NeurIPS and TIME coverage, and present at a virtual Demo Day with $7,000 in prizes plus a career fair featuring METR, Redwood Research, GovAI and MATS. Open to undergraduates, graduate/PhD students and professionals with technical or policy backgrounds; no prior research experience required.

structured.program_dates: Fall 2026 round (mentor applications June 26 – July 26, 2026; decisions July 27, 2026)

name: Coefficient Giving — Transition Grants
current_deadline: Closed – program transferred to BlueDot Impact (September 4, 2026)
current_details: Coefficient Giving's Career Development and Transition Funding provided grants to individuals at any career stage building career capital for work reducing global catastrophic risks, with particular interest in AI safety and global catastrophic biological risks. It funded graduate study, unpaid internships, independent study, career transition and exploration periods, postdocs, professional certifications, online courses, and sabbaticals, was open to applicants in any country, and had no minimum or maximum number of grants. The program was handed over to BlueDot Impact on September 4, 2026 — prospective applicants should apply through BlueDot's career transition and rapid grants programs, while existing grantees can still contact careerdevelopmentfunding@coefficientgiving.org.

structured.location: Open to applicants in any country

name: Coefficient Giving — Technical AI Safety RFP
current_details: Coefficient Giving's (formerly Open Philanthropy) request for proposals for technical AI safety research covering 21 research areas across five clusters: adversarial machine learning, sophisticated misbehavior in LLMs, model transparency, trust from first principles, and alternative approaches to mitigating AI risks. The fund expected to deploy roughly $40M over 5 months, with grants ranging from rapid API-credit funding to seed funding for new research organizations. Applications were submitted via an expression of interest form, which closed April 15, 2025, with a 3-month grace period for revise-and-resubmit and late applicants that ended July 15, 2025.

name: Foresight Institute AI Nodes
current_details: Foresight Institute's AI for Science & Safety Nodes provide grant funding, office space, community, and access to private local compute clusters at physical hubs in San Francisco and Berlin, plus a community xNode in Cape Town with the Cape Institute for Safe AI (CISAI). The current RFP spans three calls: I. Local Compute, II. Coordination and accountability, and III. AI-first science (Bio, Neuro, Nano), with grants typically between $30,000 and $100,000 (larger amounts possible for the right project). Individuals, teams, non-profits and for-profits may apply; strong priority goes to applicants who will be active, in-person contributors at the Nodes, and review takes roughly three months after the deadline.

structured.location: San Francisco & Berlin (xNode in Cape Town)

name: Long-Term Future Fund (LTFF)
current_deadline: Closed - replaced by Transformative AI Fund
current_details: The Long-Term Future Fund has been permanently closed by EA Funds and replaced by the new Transformative AI Fund. The LTFF previously made early-stage grants to individuals and organizations working to reduce catastrophic risks from advanced AI, including technical research, policy, forecasting, and field-building. A legacy LTFF page remains online but no longer accepts applications or donations — applicants and donors are directed to the Transformative AI Fund instead.

name: Manifund Regranting
current_details: Manifund's AI Safety Regranting program gives expert regrantors independent budgets of $100K–$350K to fund AI safety projects sourced from their own networks or from Manifund's open call. Because one regrantor owns each budget instead of a committee, grants can be approved in days rather than months, with example regrants ranging from $11K to $200K. Manifund's 501c3 fiscal sponsorship lets regrantors fund individuals, unregistered projects, and (pending diligence) for-profits, and all grants — including the regrantor's written rationale — are published publicly.

name: Meridian Cambridge — Research Accelerator Week
current_details: An intensive 6-day programme in Cambridge, UK (18–23 May 2026) that moves technical AI safety researchers into funded independent research via a dedicated Coefficient Giving funding pathway. Participants meet 30+ researchers to form teams, submit an EOI on Day 3, and leave with a completed grant proposal, plus fiscal sponsorship through Meridian and automatic consideration for a 3-12 month Visiting Researcher Programme residency in central Cambridge. Workspace, accommodation, meals, visa support and travel reimbursement (up to £200 UK, £400 Europe, £700 international) are covered; the previous cohort secured over $1M in funding.

structured.stipend: Costs covered (travel up to £700, accommodation, meals, visa); funding via Coefficient Giving grants

name: Schmidt Sciences — Trustworthy AI RFP
current_details: Schmidt Sciences lists its current open funding calls on this page and notes that it proactively seeks out grant opportunities and does not accept unsolicited proposals. As of this check, no Trustworthy AI / AI & Advanced Computing call is listed — the only active calls are climate-focused: Decarbonization Modeling of Urban Mobility and the Built Environment (DEVI) and Virtual Institute for the Carbon Cycle (VICC-2). Researchers can subscribe to the AI & Advanced Computing newsletter to be alerted when a new AI call opens.

name: Schmidt Sciences — Scaling AI Safety for a Multi-Agent World
current_deadline: Closed — deadline was August 9, 2026 11:59 PM AoE
current_details: A joint funding call from Schmidt Sciences, Google DeepMind, ARIA, the Cooperative AI Foundation, and Google.org supporting foundational research on safety in multi-principal, multi-agent AI ecosystems. Two tiers were offered — Tier 1 up to $300,000 and Tier 2 $300,000–$1,000,000 — for 1–2 year projects across four research clusters: sandboxes and testbeds, the science of agent networks, strengthening agent infrastructure, and multi-agent oversight and control. The call opened June 11, 2026, held informational webinars in June and July, and decisions are expected in Autumn 2026.

name: Survival & Flourishing Fund (SFF)
current_deadline: Closed — Main Round: April 22, 2026; Theme Rounds: June 10 / June 24 / July 8, 2026
current_details: The Survival and Flourishing Fund (SFF) ran its 2026 S-Process Grant Round in collaboration with Jaan Tallinn and Survival and Flourishing Corp, distributing an estimated $20–40MM+ across all rounds and tracks. The Main Round allocated $14–28MM via the Main Track ($10–20MM), Freedom Track ($2–4MM), and Fairness Track ($2–4MM), with recommendations announced September 2026; three new Theme Rounds — Climate Change, Animal Welfare, and Human Self-Enhancement & Empowerment ($2–4MM each) — announce recommendations in November 2026. Late applications are not eligible for the 2026 rounds but remain eligible for Speculation Grants and the next announced round.

structured.program_dates: Main Round recs September 2026; Theme Round recs November 2026

name: UK AISI Alignment Project
current_deadline: Closed - unlikely to run in 2026; check aisi.gov.uk/grants for future programs
current_details: The Alignment Project is a global AI alignment research fund launched in 2025 by an international coalition including the UK AI Security Institute, CAISI, CIFAR, Australia's AI Safety Institute, OpenAI, Microsoft, AWS, Anthropic, Schmidt Sciences, ARIA and UKRI. It awards grants of £50,000 to £1,000,000 to researchers across disciplines — from computer science to cognitive science — plus dedicated cloud compute and API credits, potential venture investment, and hands-on support from AISI's Alignment team. Round 1 awarded over £27 million across more than 60 projects, spanning priority areas such as interpretability, learning theory, cryptography, cognitive science and AI monitoring.

name: 5050 AI (Fifty Years)
current_details: 5050 AI is a 13-week free accelerator from Fifty Years that helps AI researchers turn their research into deep tech startups focused on AI safety and alignment, with no equity and no fees. Sessions run in SF/Boston and (in partnership with the UK's ARIA) London, plus remote, with mentors including Wojciech Zaremba, Emmett Shear, Ross Girshick, Dileep George, and Ronnie Chatterji. 340 alumni have launched 78 companies with a 95% seed raise success rate.

name: Catalyze Impact
current_details: Catalyze Impact is a 501(c)(3) non-profit incubator for AI safety, security, and resilience organizations, offering highly customized 1-on-1 support on direction & strategy, co-founder matching, mentorship from an expert network, and access to a seed funding network of grantmakers and investors, plus a stipend so founders can work full-time. Founders also join private office hours and Q&As with figures such as Jaime Sevilla (Epoch AI), Chris Akin (Apollo Research), and Eric Ho (Goodfire). The program has incubated ~15 organizations to date, with the majority raising 6 or 7 figures, spanning AI control, governance, and hardware security.

name: Halcyon Futures
current_details: Halcyon Futures is a nonprofit incubator and venture fund backing exceptional founders, operators, and researchers building in AI safety and alignment, biosecurity, AI/cybersecurity, and governance and policy. It offers career transition grants up to $500K, nonprofit seed grants up to $1M (often wired within days), and venture investments of $1M+, plus incubation, co-founder matching, introductions to frontier labs, VCs and funders, and multi-day founder retreats. Its portfolio spans 25+ launched organizations that have raised $400M+ in follow-on funding, alongside 150 supported career transitions.

structured.stipend: Up to $500K career transition grants; up to $1M nonprofit seed grants; $1M+ investments

name: ImpactOps
current_details: Impact Ops is an operations consultancy offering consultancy and hands-on specialist support to high-impact organizations across AI safety, global health and development, animal welfare, and climate change. Services cover finance (budgets to bookkeeping), recruitment, entity setup and fiscal-sponsor spin-outs, donor/grantee due diligence, operational audits, and systems implementation. Clients include the Centre for Long-Term Resilience, BlueDot Impact, Foresight Institute, Forecasting Research Institute, Longview Philanthropy, Giving What We Can, Condor Initiative, Impact Academy, and Arkose; the site also lists a Careers page and a contact form for engaging their services.

name: Rethink Priorities Special Projects
current_details: Rethink Priorities' Special Projects Program provides fiscal sponsorship and end-to-end operational support — finance and tax administration, accounting, recruitment, hiring through US/UK entities or an international Employer of Record, visa sponsorship, fundraising coordination, and event planning — so high-impact initiatives can launch and scale quickly. Fees for new projects are typically around 14% of project costs, varying with needs, complexity, and scale. Through the end of 2025 the team had received 195 expressions of interest, supported 15 projects, expended $19.7M in direct costs, onboarded 114 sponsee staff, run 16 completed hiring rounds, and completed 32 successful US/UK visa applications.

structured.location: US / UK / international via Employer of Record

name: Seldon Lab
current_details: Seldon Lab is an AI security and safety startup accelerator investing in and hands-on building with founders working exclusively on world-scale AGI deployment and existential security technologies. Beyond capital and mentorship, the team publishes papers, builds systems, and deploys cyber-physical infrastructure, with network guests including Geoff Ralston, Emmett Shear, and Josh Achiam, and a team including Eric Ries and Esben Kran. Batch #2's Demo Day was held Apr 20, 2026, and applications are accepted on a rolling basis via the site's Apply Now page.

name: WorkStream
current_details: WorkStream Nonprofit (High Impact Alliance, a 501c3) provides operations consulting, embedded implementation support, and advisory services designed to help nonprofits boost impact by 30% or more on the same budget. Its flagship six-month Operations Accelerator cohort brings together six growth-stage organizations to build sustainable systems, strategic planning skills, and end-to-end workflow optimization, with applications accepted on a rolling basis. Additional offerings include Operations Fundamentals resets, Support & Implementation integrators, GRIP and fiscal sponsorship programs, a Grant Readiness Course, an Operations Health Check, and free monthly webinars on budgeting, compliance, hiring, workflow, and fundraising.

name: 80,000 Hours Job Board
current_details: The 80,000 Hours Job Board is a continuously updated, handpicked collection of high-impact roles tackling the world's most pressing problems, including AI safety, AI policy, and existential risk reduction. Users can search and filter by salary, location, and role type, browse hiring organisations, get personalised matches based on their background, save or hide listings, and subscribe to daily or weekly job alerts. Free 1-1 career advice and extensive career research (career guide, AI careers, list of top skills, list of world problems) sit alongside the board.

name: AISafety.com Jobs
current_details: AISafety.com Jobs is a continuously updated job board currently listing 541 open roles across AI safety research, policy, engineering, operations, information security and communications. Recent listings include positions at Microsoft, Epoch AI, Kairos, Google DeepMind, Anthropic, xAI, FAR AI, Arcadia Impact, Lucid Computing, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory and the Lawfare Institute, with advertised pay ranging from roughly $48,800 to $850,000 (plus UK roles at £45,000–£144,000). Roles span entry-level to senior leadership, many remote or based in the San Francisco Bay Area, New York, London, Washington DC, Seattle and Austin, and many do not require technical skills.

structured.location: Remote (Global) & San Francisco Bay Area, New York, London, Washington DC, Seattle, Austin, Livermore

name: Center for AI Safety (CAIS)
current_details: The Center for AI Safety (CAIS) is a San Francisco-based AI safety non-profit working to reduce societal-scale risks from AI through research, field-building, and advocacy. Its careers page lists no specific open roles at present but invites interested candidates to email hiring@safe.ai with questions, and researchers can submit a collaboration form to work with CAIS.

name: FAR AI Careers
current_details: FAR AI's careers landing page invites people to join a team building trustworthy and secure AI, spanning research agendas, events convening global AI leaders, and field-building programs. The page is a high-level overview with no individual job listings, deadlines, salary, or location details — specific openings are linked elsewhere on the site and typically filled on a rolling basis.

name: MATS Alumni Hiring Database
current_details: A signup form to create an account for the MATS Alumni Hiring Database, which connects alumni of the MATS (ML Alignment & Theory Scholars) Program with organizations hiring in AI safety. Registration requires only a full name, email, and agreement to the MATS Privacy Policy. This resource is exclusively for MATS program alumni.

name: MATS Careers (Staff Hiring)
current_deadline: Oct 1, 2026 (Research Manager, for Jan 2027 start); rolling for other roles
current_details: MATS is hiring across multiple staff roles to support its AI safety research program, including General Counsel (Berkeley), Research Manager (Berkeley, London, DC — apply by Oct 1 for a January 2027 start, then rolling hiring for future cohorts), Community Manager, Head of Finance, Executive Assistant (Berkeley), Executive Business Partner (London), and Operations Generalist (Berkeley). The Research Manager role asks for 2–5 years of experience in project/research/people management, technical research, governance, or mentoring. Three recently listed roles — (Senior) Program Manager, Mentor Selection; Program Coordinator, Main Program; and Impact Analyst — carried a Sep 27, 2026 deadline that has now passed; candidates without a matching open role can submit a general Expression of Interest form.

name: What AI Safety Orgs Want in a Hire
current_details: Blog post from 80,000 Hours (published September 23rd, 2025) sharing survey results from 38 leaders of top AI safety organisations on what they look for in hires. Key takeaways: 1–3 years of relevant experience is often enough for many non-technical-research and policy roles, and the most-recommended upskilling routes are BlueDot courses, the Talos Fellowship, MATS, GovAI fellowships, the Cambridge ERA:AI Fellowship, and Pivotal Research. It stresses publishing your work publicly, networking at events like EA Global, notes hardest-to-fill profiles (chiefs of staff, policy experience, Mandarin speakers, European citizens with AI context), and points to the 80,000 Hours job board with 300+ AI safety roles.

name: Apollo Research
current_details: Apollo Research is hiring across technical research, engineering, governance, and operations for its AI security work on frontier model alignment, scheming, deception, AI control, and loss-of-control risks. Most staff are based in London or San Francisco with regular in-office collaboration and flexible hours, and benefits include competitive salary and equity, pension/401(k) matching, unlimited PTO, private medical insurance, 6 months paid parental leave, and visa sponsorship plus relocation support. Hiring runs through an application screen, a 30-minute screening call, a 2-2.5 hour take-home task, three 60-minute role-specific interviews, and a final leadership interview, with candidates typically starting within 3 months; no internships are offered and rejected applicants may re-apply after 6 months.

name: Beneficial AI Foundation
current_details: The Beneficial AI Foundation (founded by Max Tegmark) is hiring for fully remote roles focused on keeping AI beneficial for future generations. Open positions include AI Safety Research Scientist (starting at $35–$75/hour, depending on experience and qualifications) and Research Engineer (starting at $30–$70/hour, commensurate with track record and demonstrated potential). Both roles are remote from anywhere with no stated application deadline.

name: Forethought
current_details: Forethought Research is a non-profit researching how to navigate rapid AI progress and the transition to superintelligent AI, covering AI-driven progress modeling, AI-enabled coups, governance, deep space resource governance, and long-run strategy. Three openings are listed with no application deadline: a general researcher expression of interest, one focused on extreme power concentration, and a Founders Fellowship. Roles are based in Oxford or Berkeley (remote negotiable, UK/US visa sponsorship usually available), with 33 days annual leave, a £5k/yr professional development budget, 14 weeks full-pay parental leave, and a pension with 2x employer match up to £10k/yr.

name: Goodfire
current_details: Goodfire is an AI interpretability startup hiring agentic, mission-driven people to build the future of understanding AI systems, including its Silico product line for LLMs, life sciences, and robotics/vision. All roles are full-time, in person five days a week at their San Francisco (Telegraph Hill) office, with open roles listed on the careers page and filterable by team.

name: Gray Swan AI
current_details: Gray Swan AI hires across AI security research, adversarial evaluation, and red-teaming — currently highlighting Software Engineer openings — with work that has directly informed the safety evaluations of frontier models including Claude, GPT, and Gemini. Benefits include 28 days off between holidays and PTO, 401(k) with up to 4% matching, flexible work arrangements, visa sponsorship, professional development support, medical/dental/vision coverage, catered lunches at the Pittsburgh office, and 100% paid parental leave with up to 14 weeks of paid birthing leave. Open roles are listed on the careers page and reviewed on a rolling basis.

name: LawZero
current_details: LawZero is a non-profit AI safety lab founded by Yoshua Bengio, based in Montreal with a presence in Berlin, building non-agentic, safe-by-design AI to accelerate scientific discovery and provide oversight of agentic AI systems. Its Greenhouse board currently lists roughly 15 openings across research, engineering, and operations, including Director of Evaluations, Machine Learning Manager, Mathematical Scientist for AI Safety Research, ML Research Scientist (probabilistic inference), Senior ML Research Scientist, Senior ML Research Developer, Senior ML Data Processing Developer, Senior Distributed ML Engineer, Senior Data Platform Engineer, Platform Engineer, Operations Admin Lead – Executive Office, Senior Manager of Talent Acquisition, Technical Recruiter, and a Communications Specialist. A Talent Community sign-up is also available for future opportunities.

current_details: Generator is a 3-month residency in Berkeley run by Kairos and Constellation for AI safety generalists — highly agentic executors from technical, operations, policy, engineering, design or writing backgrounds — who pitch, build, and ship projects that strengthen AI safety ecosystem capacity and infrastructure. Residents receive a $6k/month stipend plus housing, travel, generous project budgets, Constellation office access and mentorship, with placement support into full-time AI safety roles afterward; selected residents are invited into a further three-month extension (roughly Sept–Nov 2026). The summer 2026 cohort of 15–30 residents ran June 15 – Aug 28, 2026; only expressions of interest for the next round are being collected now.

name: AIXI Labs Fellowship
current_details: Universal Algorithmic Intelligence (uaiasi.com) is a community hub for researchers working on Solomonoff induction, AIXI, and the mathematical foundations of intelligence, using computability theory and probability to work backward from idealized reasoning toward practical algorithms. The site hosts regular online research and paper-discussion meetings plus an "Introduction to Universal Artificial Intelligence" reading group as an on-ramp for new students and researchers from other fields. It periodically awards fellowships for UAI/AI-safety research — a recent post announces September 2026 fellowships awarded — and publishes community blog posts on topics such as imitation learning, corrigibility, and the coding theorem.

name: Frame Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed — Cohort 2.0 applications closed August 5, 2026; express interest for next cycle
current_details: The Frame Fellowship is a 10-week accelerator in San Francisco for content creators producing high-quality video that educates the public about AI and its societal and economic implications. Fellows receive housing, meals, and a $10,000 stipend, plus mentorship from creators like Rob Miles, Drew Spartz, Liron Shapira, and Petr Lebedev, across two tracks (Independent and Amplifier, the latter embedding with orgs such as MATS, Apart Research, Andon Labs, the AI Digest, The Midas Project, and CAIS). Cohort 2.0 runs September 7 – November 15, 2026; applications are closed, but an expression-of-interest form collects sign-ups for the next cycle.

name: Collective Intelligence Project Research Fellowship
current_details: The Collective Intelligence Project's pilot Research Fellowship supports 3 fellows for 6 months to conduct original research with CIP's proprietary datasets (Global Dialogues multi-country AI attitude surveys across 70+ countries, Collective Generation deliberation data, and the Weval evaluation platform) at the intersection of AI, public values, and democratic governance. It is remote and non-residential at 5–10 hours/week with bi-weekly virtual lab meetings and a fixed $9,000 stipend paid across three milestone-based tranches. Aimed primarily at late-stage PhD candidates (ABD) and early-career postdocs in political science, computational social science, sociology, or CS/ML, though independent and international scholars are welcome.

structured.program_dates: Start around early to mid-June 2026 (rolling admissions)

name: Frontier AI Security Residency
current_deadline: Not yet announced — mailing list open for the 12 Oct – 4 Dec 2026 cohort
current_details: The Frontier AI Security Residency (FASR) is an 8-week, fully funded in-person research and engineering programme in Cambridge, UK, run by ERA with Heron and the Oxford Hardware AI Governance Lab. Residents work alongside mentors from leading AI hardware and cybersecurity teams on concrete projects in hardware-enabled verification, cybersecurity and policy, running 12 Oct – 4 Dec 2026. No formal application form is live — the site currently collects interest through its mailing list, with talks, poster sessions at ERA conferences, and a live-in cohort community.

name: Heron AI Security Research Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed - express interest in future cohorts
current_details: Heron's AI Security Research Fellowship pairs experienced cybersecurity professionals (5+ years) with AI security field leaders across 10-12 collaborative research teams working on AI infrastructure and hardware security, technical AI governance, adversarial/model security, AI control and containment, and cyber evaluations. The program runs 3 months (September–November 2026), remote-first with coworking hubs in London, Tel Aviv and San Francisco, at 8-30 hours/week. It is unpaid, but teams receive $1,000+ in compute, Claude Code Team accounts, and up to $5K per team in conference travel support, with a guaranteed presentation at the AI Security Forum in Tel Aviv.

structured.stipend: Unpaid ($1,000+ compute credits; up to $5K/team travel)
structured.location: Remote-first; Tel Aviv, London, San Francisco hubs

name: CBAI AIxBiosecurity Fellowship
current_deadline: Fall 2026 round closed (Sept 6, 2026); Spring 2027 cycle applications expected to open late September 2026 — EOI form open
current_details: The CBAI AIxBiosecurity Research Fellowship is a fully-funded 10-week research program in Harvard Square, Cambridge, MA focused on AI-enabled biological risk — dangerous capability evaluations, safeguards and unlearning for bio-relevant models, threat modeling, biosurveillance, DNA synthesis screening, and governance of compute, model access and dual-use publication. Fellows receive a $15,000 stipend, housing for relocators, free weekday meals, 24/7 office access, weekly 1:1 mentorship from researchers at SecureBio, RAND, Harvard, Active Site, Protectome and LatchBio, plus ~$1,500/week in compute credits and possible extension funding up to 6 months. It runs alongside the CBAI AI Safety Research Fellowship for a combined cohort of 40 fellows; students, postdocs, recent grads and experienced professionals (as Senior Fellows) are welcome, and J-1 visa sponsorship will be available starting with the spring cycle.

name: AI Security Bootcamp — London
current_details: AI Security Bootcamp London is a 7-day intensive, fully funded program for experienced security professionals working to secure frontier AI systems, running Dec 6–12, 2026 in London. The curriculum covers threat modeling, adversarial attacks, LLM and infrastructure security, weight security and formal methods, data center security, AI control, and hardware governance via lectures, demos, and hands-on red/blue team exercises. Tuition, meals, materials, and accommodation are covered with need-based travel support; 20 participants are accepted and 5+ years of hands-on security experience is required (no prior AI/ML background needed).

structured.stipend: Fully funded (tuition, meals, accommodation covered; need-based travel support)

name: Frontier AI Security Training (FAST)
current_details: Frontier AI Security Training (FAST) is a 5-day fully funded, in-person intensive in Singapore run by SASH for 20 experienced cybersecurity and machine learning practitioners. Days cover AI model fundamentals, AI control, open-weight security (safety fine-tuning removal, data poisoning, distillation), and verification, with hands-on labs each afternoon and a final day of career mapping, funding pathways, and one-to-one instructor sessions. It is not introductory — applicants need hands-on PyTorch experience (ML4Good/ARENA level, having trained or fine-tuned a model) or deep technical security work; compliance and advisory backgrounds are not a fit.

name: FAS AI Safety Policy Entrepreneurship Fellowship
GovAI U.S. AI Policy Program
current_details: The GovAI U.S. AI Policy Program is a bipartisan, part-time, 12-week program for U.S. policy professionals in government and think tanks, building a technically-informed understanding of the AI policy landscape. It requires about 5 hours per week (3 hours of reading plus 2 hours of evening synchronous sessions, attended in person at GovAI's D.C. office near DuPont Circle or remotely) and is free of charge, with dinner provided for in-person attendees. Eligible applicants include executive and legislative branch staff, fellows, interns, detailees, military and national lab personnel, and think tank researchers, with preference for those in the D.C. metro area; completion requires attending 9 of 12 sessions, writing a policy memo or op-ed, and passing an interview-based exam.

name: Vista Institute for AI Policy
current_details: The Vista Institute for AI Policy (a fiscally sponsored project of Rethink Priorities) builds the academic field of AI law and policy through part-time virtual courses, DC workshops, and a fellowship. Its 2026 virtual courses — National Security Law and AI (Aug 10–26), AI Agents and the Law Module 1 (Aug 19–Sep 4), and Module 2 (Sep 7–Oct 2, currently running) — have all begun or concluded. The AI Law and Policy Fellowship sponsors students and recent graduates for independent research with mentors or research-assistant placements, but has no public application: completing a Vista course is what makes you eligible to apply.

name: Singapore AI Safety Hub (SASH)
current_details: The Singapore AI Safety Hub (SASH) is a Singapore-based organisation bridging governments, academia and industry across East and West on trustworthy frontier AI, with applied technical governance research in verification mechanisms, frontier safety evaluations and agent governance. It runs the Singapore AI Safety Fellowship for researchers and the Frontier AI Security Training (FAST) Policy Lab for policymakers, alongside public talks, private convenings and a co-working space in central Singapore for AI governance and safety practitioners. The site advertises open roles and states it is hiring globally, but the homepage lists no specific application windows or dates.

name: Center for Technology & Statecraft
current_details: The Center for Technology & Statecraft (CTS) is a non-partisan AI policy research initiative in Washington, DC, founded by former White House NSC and Commerce Department official Saif M. Khan. Its team of technologists, analysts, and former policymakers produces technical, forward-looking research on the AI transition, US-China competition, semiconductor supply chains, export controls, and compute infrastructure. The homepage links to a Careers page but lists no specific internship, fellowship, application window, or deadline.

structured.location: Washington, DC (1225 Union St NE, Ste 800, Washington, DC 20002)

name: Secure AI Project
current_details: Secure AI Project is a San Francisco-based AI policy and safety advocacy organization that develops and advocates for pragmatic policies to reduce risks of severe harm from advanced AI. The homepage links to About, Contact, Donate, Bills We Support, and Careers pages, but lists no specific internship, fellowship, or job openings, application windows, or deadlines. Interested applicants should monitor the Careers page for postings.

name: SAIGE Incubator — Safe AI Germany
current_deadline: Closed — Spring 2026 cohort deadline was March 22, 2026
current_details: The SAIGE Incubator is Safe AI Germany's national mentorship program pairing newcomers with expert mentors on AI safety projects across four tracks: Technical AI Safety, AI Governance & Policy, Technical AI Governance, and Communications & Field-Building. Mentees work in teams of 1–5 at 10–20 hours per week for roughly 3 months (April 27 – July 31, 2026, with an optional 3-month extension), alongside a tailored AI safety crash course, weekly mentor meetings, research skills workshops, a global speaker series, and career guidance. No prior AI safety experience is required; backgrounds in CS, maths, law, political science, psychology, economics, operations or field-building are welcome.

name: BlueDot Impact — Incubator Week
current_deadline: Cohort v6 runs November 2–6, 2026 — applications rolling
current_details: BlueDot Impact's Incubator Week is a 5-day, all-expenses-paid founder sprint in San Francisco for technically serious people in AI safety, biosecurity, cyber, or other catastrophic-risk fields: build threat models Monday, test interventions Tuesday–Wednesday, prep Thursday, and pitch Friday for up to $100k in grant funding (delivered within two weeks if you make good progress). Past cohorts total 50 participants who have raised $7M+ externally, with alumni including Exona Lab, 0Labs, Telluvian, Alma Grants, and safely.bio, plus career-transition grants and placements at Andon Labs, ASET, and BlueDot. No polished idea required — you just need to be ready to leave your current role and build; referrals earn $2,000 per accepted person.

structured.stipend: Up to $100k in grants; all expenses paid

name: Neolithic
current_details: Neolithic is a newly founded nonprofit startup in San Francisco building open-source, agentic tools and infrastructure to accelerate AI safety research, with projects spanning rogue-deployment datasets, evaluation-awareness mitigation, agent infrastructure for research, and automated reward hacking detection. It is funded to bring on its first two hires immediately, offering end-to-end project ownership and direct collaboration with researchers at leading AI safety organizations. It also invites safety researchers and orgs to request custom tooling, which Neolithic will build and maintain for free.

name: d_model
current_details: d_model is a fundamental AI research lab partnering with frontier labs to turn their models into capable interpretability and alignment researchers, building RL environments for open-ended interpretability tasks that teach agents to do cutting-edge research rather than reward-hack. The lab also pursues independent interpretability research, with publications on LLM-agent-discovered concept-erasure algorithms, how models represent program nullability, and steering characters via interpretability. Career interest is collected through a general Hiring Interest Form rather than a formal application window.

name: Allelo
current_details: Allelo is a new AI safety research initiative (fiscally sponsored by Rethink Priorities) studying what propensities and character traits make AI agents safe to deploy in complex, multi-agent, sometimes adversarial real-world settings, with an initial focus on susceptibility to influence. It aims to produce concrete agent-design recommendations for frontier labs, regulators, and certification bodies. The team is hiring a full-time Senior Researcher at USD 120,000–150,000 (higher possible for exceptional candidates), location-flexible with London preferred, and potentially convertible to a co-founder role.

name: RESI — Institute for Responsible Superintelligence
current_details: RESI (Institute for Responsible Superintelligence) is a nonprofit research institute in Cambridge, Massachusetts building the scientific foundations for superintelligence that is "safe by design," applying the cryptography playbook of precise definitions, constructions, composition, and impossibility results to AI safety. It was founded by Turing Award winner Shafi Goldwasser, cryptographer Vinod Vaikuntanathan, and former OpenAI Safety Systems researcher Adam Tauman Kalai, with participating researchers spanning computer science, mathematics, economics, and law. Research is AI-assisted from the start and organized into 11 named working groups — including formal verification (Adam Chlipala), cryptographic verification (Goldwasser), monitoring and control (Vaikuntanathan), modular architectures (Kalai), game-theoretic foundations (Yannai A. Gonczarowski), ethics (Chloé Bakalar), legal alignment (Noam Kolt), AI harnesses, and data attribution — alongside an active visitor program.

name: Verified Mechanisms
current_details: Verified Mechanisms is an independent, grant-funded research project (via Manifund) building a formally verified autoresearch pipeline for theoretical mechanistic interpretability, where multiple frontier LLM agents collaborate to generate theorems that are machine-checked in Lean 4. The pilot problem asks how many attention heads are required to compute a Boolean function, with outputs including an open-source multi-agent orchestration harness and the xorformer theorem ledger repository. The team of six researchers says it plans to onboard additional researchers over the coming months for multi-agent orchestration and mech interp work — there is no formal application form, but interested people can join the Discord or email hello@verifiedmechanisms.ai.

name: PauseAI — Vacancies
current_details: PauseAI's vacancies page lists no open positions at present, but the organisation invites spontaneous applications from people passionate about its mission to pause frontier AI development. Interested candidates can email a CV and brief cover letter to vacancies@pauseai.info; submissions are kept on file and revisited when paid roles next open, though a response is not guaranteed.

name: ML4Good Technical Bootcamp
current_deadline: Not yet announced — join notification list
current_details: ML4Good's Technical Programme is a free, residential AI safety bootcamp covering transformers from scratch, LLM agents, interpretability, RLHF, evaluations, technical governance, and a 2-day capstone project with mentorship and 1-on-1 career sessions. Food, accommodation and teaching are provided at no cost, travel may be reimbursed, and cohorts are organised regionally so participants come from the same area; all sessions run in English. It targets people with some coding experience (coding is ~25-30% of the curriculum) who are committed to contributing substantially to AI safety — alumni have gone on to MATS, SaferAI, UK AISI and the EU AI Office.

structured.stipend: Free — food, accommodation and teaching covered; travel may be reimbursed
structured.location: Regional cohorts — past locations include UK, Canada, Germany, South Africa, France, Singapore, Brazil, Italy, Colombia, Switzerland
structured.program_dates: New cohorts coming soon; most recent was UK, September 2026

name: Successif
current_details: Successif provides free, expert-guided career development for experienced professionals moving into AI risk reduction work. Support includes personalized 1:1 advising with dedicated advisors, resume/application feedback and mock interviews, expert-led workshops and self-paced courses, direct introductions to AI risk organizations with early access to jobs, and a peer community via Discord and events. Specialized tracks include an AI Policy Strategy Fellowship and a Women's Program for underrepresented groups.

name: MIT AI Risk Initiative
current_details: The MIT AI Risk Initiative is an ongoing research project producing open data and frameworks for identifying, prioritizing, and managing AI risks. Its tools include the AI Risk Repository (a living taxonomy, now at Version 4), an AI Incident Tracker, a governance database mapping global AI laws and policies to risk domains, an AI Risk Mitigation Database, an expert survey on priority risks, and the AI Risk Navigator, an interactive tool connecting all datasets via shared taxonomies. The site also publishes a blog with research updates, framework summaries, and project news, plus a newsletter to join.

name: ALIGN — AI Alignment Network
current_details: ALIGN (AI Alignment Network), a Japanese non-profit general incorporated association founded in September 2023, is recruiting volunteer staff for event operations, community management, PR/social media, research and writing, website maintenance, and organizational administration. Applicants should ideally commit 3–4+ hours per week and have basic admin/IT skills; English ability is welcomed, and depending on fit and ALIGN's finances a paid role of roughly 1–2 days per week may be discussed. Apply via the Contact form with name, affiliation, experience (100–400 characters), what you'd like to do at ALIGN (~400 characters), and availability, followed by document screening and an online interview.

structured.stipend: Volunteer; possible paid role of ~1–2 days/week depending on fit and finances

name: Vegas AI Security Forum
current_details: The Vegas AI Security Forum is an annual invite-based gathering (held during Black Hat/DEF CON week) that convenes experts in AI, cybersecurity, and national security to work on securing powerful AI models. The most recent edition, Vegas AI Security Forum '26, took place Aug 6, 2026 in Las Vegas and has concluded; the organizers' other events are still accepting applications — TLV '26 on Nov 22, 2026 in Israel and a DC Reading Group in the US. The forum is fiscally sponsored by Hack Club, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit.

structured.location: Las Vegas, USA (other editions: Tel Aviv, Washington DC, Paris)

name: ELLIS Institute Tübingen — AI Safety & Alignment Group
current_details: The AI Safety and Alignment Group at the ELLIS Institute Tübingen, led by Maksym Andriushchenko (EPFL postdoctoral researcher and ELLIS Member), develops technical solutions to reduce risks from general-purpose AI models. Research spans alignment of autonomous LLM agents, rigorous AI evaluations, public communication about frontier model capabilities and risks, and understanding how models generalize from training data. The group currently hosts four PhD students plus interns in Tübingen, Germany; this is a group overview page with no application window listed — check the institute's Careers page for open PhD and internship positions.
